nodes.summary: Adding a vector of the subspace (stratification lying in the axis span) does not change the residual.
nodes.title: Stratification within the axis span does not change the residual

nodes.summary: Residualization is additive.
nodes.title: Additivity of residualization

nodes.summary: The residual is the orthogonal projection onto `Vᗮ`.
nodes.title: Residual as projection onto the orthogonal complement

nodes.summary: The residual vanishes exactly on the subspace.
nodes.title: Residual vanishes exactly on the subspace

nodes.summary: Residuals are orthogonal to the adjustment subspace.
nodes.title: Residuals lie in the orthogonal complement

nodes.summary: Vectors orthogonal to the subspace are their own residuals: stratification outside the axis span is not removed.
nodes.title: Vectors orthogonal to the subspace are their own residuals

nodes.summary: Residualization is homogeneous.
nodes.title: Homogeneity of residualization

nodes.summary: Regressing on an orthonormal family of axes one axis at a time gives the joint residual: `y - ∑ₖ ⟪aₖ, y⟫ aₖ`.
nodes.title: Residual with respect to an orthonormal family of axes

nodes.summary: The adjusted (residualized) `y`: the residual of the least-squares regression of `y` on the subspace `V` (`y` minus its orthogonal projection onto `V`).
nodes.title: Residualized vector after adjustment for a subspace

nodes.summary: The allele-frequency estimate `p̂ⱼ = μⱼ / 2` of marker `j`, where `μⱼ` is the mean variant-allele count of column `j` (autosomal diploid data, counts in `{0, 1, 2}`).
nodes.title: Allele-frequency estimate of a marker

nodes.summary: Each of the top `K` axes lies in their span.
nodes.title: Each top axis lies in the span of the top axes

nodes.summary: The axes of variation: an orthonormal eigenbasis of `Ψ`, in decreasing eigenvalue order.
nodes.title: Axes of variation

nodes.summary: The eigenvalues of `Ψ` in decreasing order, matching `axes`.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of the axes of variation

nodes.summary: Adding vectors of `V` to the phenotype and the genotype does not change the EIGENSTRAT statistic.
nodes.title: Stratification in the axis span is removed

nodes.summary: The EIGENSTRAT statistic is nonnegative when `K + 1 ≤ N`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the EIGENSTRAT statistic

nodes.summary: A genotype lying in the axis span carries no signal after adjustment (its residual is zero, and the statistic is the junk value `0` of the zero denominator).
nodes.title: Genotypes in the axis span carry no signal after adjustment

nodes.summary: The EIGENSTRAT association statistic `(N - K - 1) ⟪r_g, r_y⟫² / (‖r_g‖² ‖r_y‖²)` of the adjusted genotype `r_g` and adjusted phenotype `r_y`: `(N - K - 1)` times their squared cosine, which is their squared sample correlation when both are centered (Price et al. 2006). When either adjusted vector is zero the ratio is the junk value `0`.
nodes.title: EIGENSTRAT association statistic

nodes.summary: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell, existence: the coefficient of the residual-on-residual regression gives a least-squares decomposition of `y` on `V ⊔ span {g}`.
nodes.title: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem, existence

nodes.summary: The top `K` axes span a `K`-dimensional subspace.
nodes.title: Dimension of the span of the top axes

nodes.summary: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell, uniqueness: in any least-squares decomposition `y = c + β g + e` with `c ∈ V` and `e ⊥ V ⊔ span {g}`, the coefficient `β` is the coefficient of the regression of the residualized `y` on the residualized `g`, and the residual `e` is the residual of that regression.
nodes.title: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem, uniqueness

nodes.summary: Residuals are orthogonal to every vector of the subspace, in particular to every axis.
nodes.title: Residuals are orthogonal to every axis

nodes.summary: The first `numSignificant stat t K` indices are exactly those `k < K` whose statistics and all earlier ones exceed the threshold.
nodes.title: Characterization of the axes counted as significant

nodes.summary: Every axis counted as significant has a statistic above the threshold.
nodes.title: Significant axes have statistics above the threshold

nodes.summary: If, under the null hypothesis, the `k`-th statistic exceeds `t` with probability at most `1 - F t` (the Tracy–Widom approximation with `F` the TW₁ distribution function, taken here as a hypothesis), then the rule declares more than `k` significant axes with probability at most `1 - F t`.
nodes.title: Conditional error bound

nodes.summary: Patterson's normalized genotype matrix `(C i j - μⱼ) / √(p̂ⱼ (1 - p̂ⱼ))`. For a monomorphic marker (`p̂ⱼ ∈ {0, 1}`) the denominator is `0` and the column is the junk value `0`; Patterson et al. use polymorphic markers only.
nodes.title: Patterson's normalized genotype matrix

nodes.summary: A higher threshold declares no more axes significant.
nodes.title: Count of significant axes decreases with the threshold

nodes.summary: For decreasing statistics (such as ordered eigenvalues compared with a fixed threshold) the sequential count is the number of statistics above the threshold.
nodes.title: Significant-axis count for decreasing statistics

nodes.summary: At most `K` axes are declared significant.
nodes.title: At most K axes are declared significant

nodes.summary: At least one axis is significant iff the leading statistic exceeds the threshold.
nodes.title: Criterion for at least one significant axis

nodes.summary: Patterson's sequential count of significant axes: among the first `K` statistics, the length of the leading run of statistics exceeding the threshold `t` (testing stops at the first non-significant one).
nodes.title: Sequential count of significant axes

nodes.summary: The all-ones vector is in the kernel of `Ψ` (columns of the normalized matrix are centered), so at most `N - 1` eigenvalues are nonzero.
nodes.title: All-ones vector lies in the kernel of the relatedness matrix

nodes.summary: Patterson's matrix `Ψ` is positive semidefinite.
nodes.title: Patterson's relatedness matrix is positive semidefinite

nodes.summary: Patterson's `N × N` matrix `Ψ = M Mᵀ / (number of markers)` of the normalized genotypes, whose top eigenvectors are the axes of variation.
nodes.title: Patterson's relatedness matrix

nodes.summary: The span of the top `K` axes of variation, the subspace EIGENSTRAT adjusts for.
nodes.title: Span of the top axes of variation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
